messages.author: d0591fb2a98d1e44
messages.subject: uniform prior on a matrix?
parts: Is there a uniform prior that I can use that will produce a random matrix? It doesn't have to be symmetric or positive definite.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] uniform prior on a matrix?
parts:
No.  The space of unconstrained matrices is isomorphic
to R^{N^{2}} so the equivalent statement would be if there
is a normalizeable uniform prior on R^{M}, which there is not.
On Jul 31, 2015, at 12:41 PM, Daniel Berman <daniel....@gmail.com> wrote:
Is there a uniform prior that I can use that will produce a random matrix? It doesn't have to be symmetric or positive definite.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] uniform prior on a matrix?
parts:
No. There are lots of ways you can constrain it to be proper.

You can draw a random N x N correlation matrix uniformly. And then
you can draw N scales (std deviations) and generate a random matrix.
Or you can use something like a Wishart prior. You can read up on
how the Wishart is based on randomly generating matrices from normal
random vectors:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wishart_distribution#Definition

- Bob
